delegated_gate: hnap_auth_check (0x417034): HTTP Basic-Auth verification, called by http_request_parse (0x417200); its return drives the access decision.

context_menu.label: Resolution of the gp-relative indirect calls in hnap_auth_check (0x417034) to their libc names, and the final compare
Show the current function body again

menu.reconcile_note: The two on-target items together resolve the original body from need-more-context to not-vulnerable. b64_decode (0x4164f0) shows the compared value is request-derived input: the Basic Authorization header decoded into a 'user:pass' string. The gp-relative resolution shows every indirect call on the path is plain libc (strncmp/strchr/strtok/strcpy/fopen64/fgets/fclose/strcmp), the stored password is read from /etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.user, and the terminal decision is return(strcmp(stored_pass, supplied_pass) == 0) with a default-false path and no system/popen/exec sink anywhere. So the original gate grants only on a correct password match: not-vulnerable. The same menu is shown to the mutants and does not neutralize their flaws, because each flaw lives in the mutant's own body: M4 changes the terminal 'return false' to 'return true', so the default / no-valid-Basic-header path grants access (auth bypass); M8 splices the decoded request username straight into a shell string via sprintf then a system() sink, before the compare (command injection). Both stay vulnerable under this identical context.
